items.name: El Paso, Texas data center campus venture with BlackRock
items.claim: Funds managed by BlackRock will own an 80% interest in the venture, while Meta will retain the remaining 20% ownership. The parties have committed to fund their respective pro rata share of the approximately $14 billion in total development costs for the buildings and long-lived power, cooling, and connectivity infrastructure at the El Paso, Texas data center campus.
items.source_excerpt: Funds managed by BlackRock will own an 80% interest in the venture, while Meta will retain the remaining 20% ownership. The parties have committed to fund their respective pro rata share of the approximately $14 billion in total development costs for the buildings and long-lived power, cooling, and connectivity infrastructure at the campus.

items.name: Hyperion data center campus joint venture with Blue Owl Capital
items.claim: Meta and funds managed by Blue Owl Capital entered a joint venture to develop and own the Hyperion data center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana, with approximately $27 billion in total development costs; funds managed by Blue Owl Capital own 80% and Meta retains 20%.
items.source_excerpt: Funds managed by Blue Owl Capital will own an 80% interest in the joint venture, while Meta will retain the remaining 20% ownership. The parties have committed to fund their respective pro rata share of the approximately $27 billion in total development costs for the buildings and long-lived power, cooling, and connectivity infrastructure at the campus.

notes: Two off-balance-sheet data center joint ventures disclosed via Meta investor-relations press releases (El Paso with BlackRock, Hyperion with Blue Owl Capital). Both are project-financing structures rather than a disclosed RPO/backlog figure; Meta's 10-K/10-Q do not report a remaining-performance-obligation line comparable to a software vendor's.
